queries.query: I need to reproduce issue #415 where CI times out waiting for units to go idle. Can you set up an experiment on the testing model that shows the uniter queue saturation?
Simulate a quorum loss on our mysql-k8s cluster so we can verify the recovery runbook actually works.
We need to test the charm's self-healing: kill one of the mysqld processes in a way that the cluster has to fail over, then observe.
Help me write a test that reliably puts the cluster in NO_QUORUM state before running promote-to-primary force. The kubectl delete pod approach keeps healing itself.
Reproduce the DNS race from issue #327 deterministically: the relation setup should fail like the original bug but reliably.
I want to verify our error-path logging change fires when the charm can't reach mysqld. How do we force that failure on the live model?
Set up a chaos experiment: take two of three units' mysqld down abruptly and check that promote-to-primary force=true succeeds.
Design an experiment for the testing model where the cluster is in stable no_quorum, then walk through the manual recovery.
We're testing a charm fix for the poisoned-retry bug. Build a repro on the live deployment where a relation setup fails mid-way exactly like issue #327.
How do we inject a durable mysqld death on k8s without the StatefulSet undoing it? Then observe what the charm does.
For our game day we need to break the mysql cluster on purpose: first a single member, then a majority. Plan the kill sequence.
Verify that the charm's manual rejoin path works: make a member get expelled from the group and watch it rejoin.
